cohort: A sample of 3,624 married mothers aged 15-49 years was analyzed, focusing on the mortality of their most recent child aged 0-12 months.
finding: Maternal education, maternal employment status, and postnatal care were significantly associated with infant mortality, while women's autonomy, household economic status, delivery method, quality of antenatal care, and birth assistance were not.
mod_finding: Delivery method showed no significant association with infant mortality (p=0.856; OR=0.9).
